question: Do the commons' checker and index builder stay fast, and its folders and pages stay inside GitHub's limits, at 10, 1,000 and 10,000 dossiers?
machine: cloud-linux-4cpu: the cloud container this session ran in (Linux, 4 vCPUs, about 16 GB of memory)

metrics.name: check_all
metrics.what: node scripts/check.mjs --all over the whole synthetic commons

metrics.name: check_pr
metrics.what: node scripts/check.mjs --base main, a pull request that adds one dossier

metrics.name: build_index
metrics.what: node scripts/build-index.mjs into an empty folder

metrics.name: store_bytes
metrics.what: total size of the files under dossiers/

metrics.name: largest_page_bytes
metrics.what: size of the largest Markdown page the index builder writes

metrics.name: largest_folder_entries
metrics.what: the most entries in any one folder under dossiers/

design: Each case builds a fresh temporary git repository: the real schemas, tag lists and template, plus n copies of one generated and filled-in dossier (about 5 KB each: one source, one claim, one finding). Copies get new ids, dates spread evenly from 2016-01-01 to 2026-11-23, and tags drawn with a fixed seed. Everything is committed except the one new dossier of the check_pr case, dated 2026-11-24. Timings are wall-clock for a child Node process, so they include Node's start-up. Size metrics are measured once per case (iteration 1, phase measure).
threats: Synthetic dossiers are far smaller than real ones (the first real dossier is about 700 KB), so store_bytes is a floor, not an estimate of a real commons. A real dossier's CSVs are longer, which makes check_all slower; check_pr reads only one dossier's CSVs, so it is less affected. One machine, one run.
replaces: 2026-11-24-scale. That run's synthetic dossiers carried dates after the run day, so every check_all and check_pr row failed: the checker rightly refused 'checked' dates in the future and printed thousands of errors, which also slowed it. The tools were not changed between the runs; only the synthetic dates were. Its build_index and size rows are kept as they came.
